# parity-fuzz --mode printf baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode printf --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# No known gaps. This mode was INFORMATIONAL (continue-on-error, no baseline)
# for a long stretch because it was gap-rich across many distinct format
# classes; it is now a blocking gate — 10,000 cases run clean.
#
# What closed it was getkeystring (c:Src/utils.c:6915), which printf drives
# through two flag sets no other caller uses (c:zsh.h:3181-3183):
#   GETKEYS_PRINTF_FMT = OCTAL_ESC|BACKSLASH_C|PRINTF_PERCENT  (the format)
#   GETKEYS_PRINTF_ARG = BACKSLASH_C                           (a %b argument)
# The bits are what make the two behave DIFFERENTLY on the same input, and
# each was wrong:
#   - `\777` (511) truncates to its low byte 0xff (c:7170 assigns a zlong to a
#     char); a u8 parse errored and emitted NOTHING at all. `\400` is NUL.
#   - `%b`'s argument has no OCTAL_ESC, so `\777` must come back as a LITERAL
#     backslash + digits (c:7157-7161 `*t++ = '\\', s--; continue;`) while the
#     FORMAT decodes the same text to a byte.
#   - Neither set has GETKEY_EMACS, so `\E` stays literal (c:7018-7024).
#   - `\u` with no hex digits emits codepoint 0 (c:7085 `wval = 0`), not
#     nothing.
#   - `%` produced by a numeric escape is doubled under PRINTF_PERCENT
#     (c:7172-7173).
#
# The divergence this mode found was a real port bug and is FIXED:
#
#   `%n` was a no-op. C stores the byte count emitted so far into a named
#   variable (c:Src/builtin.c:5427-5429):
#
#       case 'n':
#           if (curarg) setiparam(curarg, count - rcount);
#           break;
#
#       $ printf 'abc%n' v; print -r -- "[$v]"
#       zsh    abc[3]
#       zshrs  abc[]        (v never set)
#
#   printf_format is a pure formatter with no shell handle, so it now collects
#   (name, byte_count) pairs and bin_print does the setiparam. Three subtleties,
#   each pinned:
#     - `count - rcount` (c:5168 resets rcount per format-reuse cycle) means the
#       count is bytes since THIS cycle began: `printf 'x%n' a b` sets both to
#       1, not 1 and 2.
#     - `if (curarg)` tests that an arg SLOT exists, not that it is non-empty —
#       an empty or malformed name still reaches setiparam and errors `not an
#       identifier`; only a wholly absent arg is the no-op.
#     - the count is BYTES, so a multibyte literal before `%n` counts its
#       encoded length (`héllo%n` → 6).
#
#   `%n` was simply absent from PF_CONV, so it was never generated. The rest of
#   the conversion set (d i o u x X e E f g G s c b q %) all worked, so printf
#   looked covered.
#
# INTEGER OVERFLOW in a `%d`/`%i`/`%x`/`%o`/`%u` operand (fixed in math.rs): the
# arg pool only held small ints (`-20..40`), so the overflow boundary was never
# compared. printf evaluates the operand with `mathevali`, and its lexer had an
# ad-hoc `int_str[..18]` truncation shadowing the faithful `zstrtol` port
# (c:Src/utils.c:2466-2515). zstrtol accumulates the magnitude in a u64 and
# truncates ONLY on real unsigned overflow, then reinterprets the retained u64
# as signed:
#   - `9999999999999999999` (fits u64, not i64): signed-overflow special case,
#     18-digit cut, `999999999999999999` (positive).
#   - `18446744073709551615` (u64::MAX): 19-digit cut, `1844674407370955161`.
#   - `99999999999999999999` (>u64): 19-digit cut with the retained u64 read as
#     signed, `-8446744073709551617` (NEGATIVE wrap).
# The old `[..18]` cut was one digit short on the count AND returned the wrong
# (positive) value past u64. The fix delegates to `zstrtol_underscore`, matching
# the hex branch. A self-contained probe folds the `number truncated after N
# digits` stderr warning via `2>&1`; reverting the fix yields 132 divergences on
# seed 7. Bug #350 / #1013.
#
# Any divergence here is a regression.
